decisions.rationale: Reproduced by the reconciler in a scratch copy of the reviewed snapshot (commit 402c4853) with the private reference overlay. The reference with only dev-auth.js reverted to the shipped 'enabled: true' (private mutant a8) fails t3 through t8 (6 failed | 2 passed), all with 'Unable to find role="heading" and name "Sign in to Beacon"'. The README discloses only the t1/task 2 coupling, and line 103 is false while auto-sign-in is on. Reordering so dev-auth becomes task 1 would rename the failingTests names, so instead isolate the tests. Fix: (1) in tests t3, t4, t5, t6 and t7, add vi.mock('../starter/src/dev-auth.js', () => ({ devAutoSignIn: { enabled: false, session: null } })) so each starts signed out regardless of task 8. t8, unmocked, stays the only check on dev-auth.js. (2) README 'How to test': state that t8 alone checks the auto-sign-in switch, and correct line 103 so it reads as true. Verified: a8 then fails only t8; the reference passes 8/8; the shipped starter still fails all 8 under the same names. The same fix closes sme-ar-5.

Verified. Both review topic.json files record lab 'none'. module.json says the lab covers 'the four S34 topics'. A value-free diff of the private reference against the starter shows the learner adds no import or export statement, no spread, no map and no filter; NotAllowedNotice is in the same file as AdminPage. The only effect is in given use-authed-fetch.js. So the note's 'exercised as scored production work ... ES modules appear throughout' is false. Rule-6 order applied. What was verified: none of the 8 tasks as written makes the learner write an import/export, spread, map or filter, and destructuring and arrow functions are never forced by any test. Scoring those clauses would need new starter structure or task work beyond strengthening an existing test, and a partial note for #o1 would name no scored clause. So removal is the reached last resort for javascript-fundamentals-review#o3 and #o1. Fix in lab.json: (1) remove javascript-fundamentals-review#o1 and #o3 from 'objectives'. (2) Keep #o2 with a partial-objective note: scored for tracing awaited fetch calls and handling non-2xx responses as status-carrying errors in authFetch, LoginPage and handleRestart (t1, t2, t6). (3) Keep react-review#o1 with a partial-objective note. Scored: state, context, routing (Navigate/location.state) and form submission applied together, plus the state-update and changed-context-value re-render triggers (t1, t3, t6, t7). Not scored: effects and the parent-re-render trigger. (4) Rewrite the false sentence in cleanup.notes. Keep both review topics in 'covers', since each keeps one objective. topic.json and module.json stay unchanged, per the html-css-js precedent. A grep finds the same ids in react/assessments/web-and-react-module-check/blueprint.json and intake.md. Those bind the course assessment and the plan, not this lab, and need no change. Not escalated: review pages add no new syllabus, so narrowing the claim is an in-lane correction.

Verified. (a) Task 5 asks for no learner edit; the clear-and-redirect loop is given code. The learner-written 401 branch in handleRestart is unasserted: mutant a2 (every error treated as 403) passes 8/8. No clause distinguishes the server ending an HttpOnly cookie session. (b) handling-401#o1's 'state the general HTTP meanings' clause cannot be machine-scored. (c) t8 sends no unauthenticated request, so turning-off-the-dev-profile#o3 is unscored. Fix: (1) the sme-ar-2 change to t6 scores the learner's 401 branch. (2) Strengthen the existing t8: after the app opens signed out, assert that authFetch('/services', { token: null }) rejects with status 401. This scores '#o3 an unauthenticated request is now refused' against the stubbed secured API. (3) Add partial-objective notes in lab.json cleanup.notes. handling-401#o1: the apply clause is scored by t5/t6, while the 'state the meanings' clause stays on the topic page. #o2: clear-and-redirect is scored, partly through given code, and the HttpOnly-cookie distinction is page-only. turning-off-the-dev-profile#o3: refusal is verified against the stub, not a real Spring back end. Keep the existing #o2 note.

Reproduced by the reconciler in a scratch copy of the reviewed snapshot (commit 402c4853) with the private reference overlay. A module-level const read of import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL (private mutant a6) fails only t8. The react topic page turning-off-the-dev-profile (artifact.md lines 26 and 67) shows a module-level 'const searchUrl = import.meta.env.VITE_SEARCH_URL'. The html-css-js environment-settings page teaches that Vite replaces import.meta.env.VITE_* at build time and that the dev server needs a restart after .env changes. Keep the call-time requirement in t8, but fix the wording in starter/src/api.js TASK 8 and README troubleshooting: say the call-time read is a testability requirement (vi.stubEnv changes import.meta.env during the run), and that in a real Vite app the value is fixed at build or dev-server start, so changing VITE_API_URL needs a restart or rebuild.
